According to the USDA and food safety experts, cooked rice is safe to eat for 3 to 4 days if it is refrigerated promptly and stored properly. http://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/leftovers-and-food-safety
note_text: The post shares a video and expresses surprise about rice storage rules. Without seeing the video content, the poster is sharing what they learned rather than making an authoritative factual claim. The 24-hour timeframe, while more conservative than necessary, isn't dangerously incorrect - it's overly cautious. Cooked rice can safely be refrigerated for 3-6 days when stored properly.
search_results:
The claim that cooked rice must be thrown out after **24 hours** is incorrect; authoritative food safety guidelines and rice industry sources state it can be safely refrigerated for **3–7 days** (depending on the source) when stored properly in an airtight container and cooled promptly.[1][2][3][4][5]

**Key contradictions from sources directly addressing cooked rice storage:**
- Riceland Foods: Refrigerate in an airtight container for **up to 4–6 days**; never leave at room temperature more than **2 hours** to prevent bacteria.[1] (https://www.riceland.com/the-riceland-blog/the-ultimate-guide-to-storing-and-reheating-rice-tips-tricks-from-riceland-foods)
- USA Rice: Refrigerate cooked rice for **3–5 days** (home use) or **up to 7 days** (foodservice); cool to 70°F within 2 hours, then to 40°F within 4 more hours per USDA.[2] (https://www.usarice.com/thinkrice/how-to/how-to-store-rice)
- Mahatma Rice: Refrigerate cooked rice for **up to 6 days**.[3] (https://mahatmarice.com/faqs/storage/)
- Healthline (citing studies): Cooked rice keeps for **3–4 days** in the fridge (some sources say up to a week); freeze up to 8 months.[4] (https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/does-rice-go-bad)
- FoodSafety.gov (USDA chart): Aligns with 3–7 day fridge storage for cooked rice and grains when held at 41°F or below.[5] (https://www.foodsafety.gov/food-safety-charts/cold-food-storage-charts)

The 24-hour limit may stem from a misunderstanding of the **2-hour room-temperature rule** (to avoid *Bacillus cereus* bacteria), but refrigeration extends safety far beyond that.[1][2] Always check for off smells, mold, or sliminess before consuming.
